        ### Question
        Indicate which of the following will be the most likely diagnosis if an individual has a lipoprotein lipase deficiency:

        ### Options
        opa. Type I dyslipidemia
opb. Type IIa dyslipidemia.
opc. Type III dyslipidemia.
opd. Abetalipoproteinemia.
ope. Tangier disease.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency -> decreased breakdown of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins -> elevated chylomicrons and VLDL -> Type I dyslipidemia -> 80%
CHAIN: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency -> impaired clearance of chylomicron remnants -> elevated cholesterol and triglycerides -> Type III dyslipidemia -> 70%
CHAIN: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency -> reduced conversion of VLDL to LDL -> elevated LDL cholesterol -> Type IIa dyslipidemia -> 60%
CHAIN: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency -> impaired chylomicron assembly -> decreased ApoB-containing lipoproteins -> Abetalipoproteinemia -> 50%
CHAIN: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency -> dysfunctional HDL metabolism -> decreased HDL levels -> Tangier disease -> 40%

(Lipoprotein Lipase Deficiency, Familial)-CAUSES->(Hypoxia)-ASSOCIATED_WITH->(neuropeptide Y|NPY)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Myocytes, Smooth Muscle)-INTERACTS_WITH->(chylomicron remnant)
